title: Polyester & viscose yarn prices decline in India amid sluggish demand
summary:
Polyester and viscose yarn prices fell across major Indian markets as weak demand, payment constraints and lower raw material costs hit sentiment.
Ludhiana and Surat saw polyester yarn weaken, while viscose yarn eased in Mumbai and Surat on subdued buying and higher imports.
North Indian cotton prices also eased as post-Diwali arrivals rose and falling ICE futures weighed on exporters.

title: Germany's leading economic index slips 0.2% in September 2026
summary:
Germany's Leading Economic Index fell 0.2 per cent in September 2026 to 88.4, after an upwardly revised 0.8 per cent rise in August.
The six-month LEI rose 1.6 per cent from March to September, reversing a 0.5 per cent contraction in the prior six months.
The CEI also eased 0.2 per cent to 102.9, with its six-month decline widening to 0.3 per cent.

title: India ITME 2026 to showcase textile technology in Greater Noida
summary:
India ITME 2026 will bring textile machinery and technology providers to Greater Noida from 4–9 December for its 12th edition.
Covering spinning to garment manufacturing, the exhibition will spotlight automation, sustainability and modernisation.
Textile Horizons on 5–6 December will feature a CEO conclave, technical awards and networking, with over 250 decision-makers and delegates expected.

title: Nylon 6 chip prices ease 2.5% WoW despite rising caprolactam costs
summary:
China’s domestic Nylon 6 chips (HS grade) fell 2.5 per cent over the past week to $1.896/kg on November 17, 2026, as soft benzene and weaker crude dragged values lower.
Caprolactam, the direct feedstock, rose 3.2 per cent to $1.762/kg, squeezing mill margins while polymer sellers competed for orders.
Benzene declined across Asia, pointing to thin buying interest amongst converters.

title: 121 mn carbon allowances: Can Europe strengthen its textile industry?
summary:
The European Union will provide about 121 million additional free Emissions Trading System (ETS) allowances for energy-intensive installations in 2026–2030, affecting upstream textile inputs.
Most fibres, yarns, fabrics and garments remain outside CBAM, so no added carbon charges apply under the agreement.
Eligibility also requires energy-efficiency audits and climate-neutrality plans.

title: Viscose prices flat: Who blinks first, pulp or yarn mills?
summary:
China’s VSF market stayed in a tight band during 9–16 November 2026, with muted buying from downstream yarn mills and cost resistance keeping trade quiet.
Domestic 1.2D and 1.5D grades edged up 0.09 per cent, while high-end fibre eased by November 16 and medium-grade fibre fell 0.18 per cent.
Dissolving pulp offers CIF China were unchanged despite an upward bias after October’s rise.

title: US' import & export prices rise 1.1% in October
summary:
US import prices increased 1.1 per cent in October, matching September’s rise, as nonfuel imports drove the advance, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said.  
Export prices also rose 1.1 per cent after a 2.4 per cent gain in September.  
Consumer goods import prices excluding automotives rose 0.5 per cent; export prices for the category increased 0.6 per cent, led partly by apparel and footwear.

title: US-China 30-for-30 trade framework: Why is apparel still excluded?
summary:
US-China 30-for-30 tariff lists worth about $30 billion each exclude apparel, leaving China-made garments without immediate duty relief for US importers and brands.
Potential relief is limited to 19 home-textile tariff lines, with eligibility tied to HTSUS descriptions, fibre and construction.
Section 301 exclusions and maritime-action suspension expire separately in January 2027.

title: ICE cotton futures recover marginally on bargain buying, firm grains
summary:
ICE cotton futures recovered modestly, with March 2027 up 48 points at 81.40 cents per pound, but gains stayed limited by a firm US dollar.
Bargain buying, stronger grains and higher crude oil supported prices after Monday’s sharp fall near recent lows.
Volume fell to 70,485 contracts, certified stocks rose to 84,978 bales, and traders watched December liquidation before November 23.

title: Japan’s GDP contracts 0.1% in Q3, first decline in a year
summary:
Japan's real GDP shrank 0.1 per cent year-on-year in July-September, the first contraction in four quarters, Cabinet Office data showed.
The result missed a 0.3 per cent expansion forecast; quarter-on-quarter GDP was flat after 0.4 per cent growth in Q2.
Private consumption fell 0.3 per cent again as rain and living costs hit spending; government spending also fell after five quarters of growth.

title: India’s apparel exports to US fall 20.5%: Can it win back buyers?
summary:
India’s readymade garment exports rose 20.33 per cent year on year to $1.287 billion in October 2026, but April-October exports remained 2.97 per cent lower and US-bound shipments fell sharply.
The rebound follows a weak October 2025 base, with the latest value only 4.8 per cent above October 2024.
No India-specific US tariff advantage is confirmed without an implemented apparel schedule.

title: US' Amer Sports raises 2026 outlook as Q3 revenue climbs 24%
summary:
Amer Sports raised its FY26 revenue growth outlook to 25-26 per cent after third-quarter revenue increased 24 per cent to $2.17 billion. 
Net income attributable to equity holders rose 67 per cent to $240 million, while adjusted operating margin improved to 16.4 per cent. 
Technical Apparel and Outdoor Performance posted revenue growth of 26 per cent and 27 per cent, respectively.

title: China takes 34.29% of EU27 extra-EU apparel imports: Can it hold?
summary:
EU27 extra-EU apparel imports fell 2.46 per cent to €70.72 billion (~$77.7 billion) in January-September 2026, while China’s share rose to 34.29 per cent.
China’s import value grew 4.46 per cent to €24.25 billion and Vietnam’s rose 4.33 per cent to €3.47 billion.
Bangladesh fell 11.91 per cent to €13.48 billion, with share down to 19.06 per cent from 21.10 per cent.

title: Could Bangladesh’s ongoing labour protest impact sourcing dynamics?
summary:
Bangladesh garment protests have shut around 65 factories in Savar, Ashulia and Gazipur as workers seek a minimum wage rise to Taka 32,000 (~$256).
Another 56 reportedly declared holidays, deepening disruption after an energy crisis in a sector employing over four million and earning 80 per cent of merchandise exports.
Sustained delays could divert orders to India and hit Indian yarn suppliers.

title: US' Nike previews future innovations across sports and lifestyle
summary:

The company also previewed Nike Sportswear concepts including Therma-FIT A.I.R., Project Ride and Nike Morpho X.

title: Jordan's apparel exports rise 3.2% to $1.69 bn in Jan–Aug 2026
summary:
Jordan’s apparel exports rose 3.2 per cent year on year to JOD 1.196 billion (~$1.69 billion) in January–August 2026, led by knitted clothing.
Knitted apparel exports increased 4.6 per cent to JOD 1.177 billion and made up 98.3 per cent of clothing exports; woven exports fell 41.3 per cent.
August clothing exports rose 5.3 per cent, while apparel imports grew 2.8 per cent in the eight months.

title: US' Nike to launch Tuned Air running footwear in late 2027
summary:
Nike has unveiled Tuned Air, a proprietary digital-print and selective-lamination platform designed to give athletes tailored cushioning, comfort, durability and responsiveness across sports.
The technology has cut average new Air-unit development time by 70 per cent at Nike’s Advanced Product Creation Center, with runner availability planned for late 2027 before a broader rollout.

title: What drove Israel’s Delta Galil to record Q3 sales of $599.6 mn?
summary:
Delta Galil Industries posted record third-quarter 2026 sales of $599.6 million, up 11 per cent YoY, as DTC revenue grew 16 per cent. 
Net income increased 17 per cent to $36.6 million and adjusted EBIT rose 23 per cent to $63.1 million. 
The Israeli apparel group expects FY26 results to reach the middle to high end of its guidance range.

title: 65 Bangladesh RMG factories shut: Can 2027 orders stay on track?
summary:
Bangladesh's RMG minimum stays at Tk12,500 (~$100) until a new rate is notified, as the Minimum Wage Board considers a worker-side Tk32,000 proposal for the lowest regular grade.
The employers' proposal meeting was postponed to November 23; BGMEA reported 65 factories indefinitely closed by November 15.
RMG exports reached $38.70 billion in fiscal 2025–26, equal to 80.6 per cent of merchandise exports.

title: Bangladesh's RMG wage board to discuss wage proposal on November 23
summary:
Bangladesh's Minimum Wage Board will hold its third garment-sector wage meeting on November 23, after the November 16 session was postponed.
Owners' representatives had been due to submit a written minimum-wage proposal; workers' representatives earlier sought Tk32,000 (~$257) a month.
Unrest has continued in Savar, Ashulia and Gazipur over a Tk30,000 (~$241) demand.
